referees.quote: The authors have made a good case for the explanation with the support of theoretical calculations. Overall, the paper is novel in characterizing an electrically controlled interphase magnetism.

I cannot recommend publication of this work in Nature Communications in its current stage. Below I elaborate on my criticisms and can consider this manuscript again if the authors address my criticisms.

note: There is no sign of a transfer from another journal; Version 0 is the first round. R1 gives no explicit verdict. Their report is positive and asks only for clarifications (origin of the tunneling gap, why the features are small, ruling out Landau levels), so I inferred minor revision. R2 declines publication 'in its current stage' but offers to reconsider. They raise substantive challenges, such as how FGT is accessed given zero states at Gamma and ruling out tip-induced quantum-dot states, and ask for comparison with prior work. I read this as major revision rather than reject. Both referees recommended publication in Version 1.
